profile.topic: Performance track: complementary hybrid algorithms (synthetic onboarding example)

candidates.claim: Using VPGBFRS dependency weights inside a three-way reject head improves macro-F1 over both bases at equal coverage.
candidates.search_trace: Local snapshot only; searched component names, not a full external novelty review.
candidates.difference: The combination changes the decision rule and feature weighting; it is not a score concatenation.
candidates.risk: Three-way rejection can improve accuracy by lowering coverage; coverage must be fixed.
candidates.first_probe: Pilot 3 datasets x 3 seeds, same split and budget.
candidates.advance_if: At least 2/3 datasets beat both bases by >=1.0% macro-F1 at equal coverage.
candidates.stop_if: Gain disappears at equal coverage or under remove-one ablation.

component_sources.variable-precision fuzzy rough weighting: VPGBFRS (ASOC 2025): variable-precision fuzzy rough dependency weights, read from the local paper snapshot.
component_sources.three-way reject threshold: 3W-GBSVM++ (ASOC 2026): three-way decision head with a calibrated reject band, read from the local paper snapshot.

rejected_pairs.reason: Concatenation only stacks two score vectors; it adds no decision rule and is already the naive baseline, so a win would not test the claim.

rejected_pairs.pair: three-way threshold calibrated on in-sample scores
rejected_pairs.reason: In-sample calibration leaks labels and manufactures a coverage gain that cannot survive held-out evaluation.

rejected_pairs.pair: VPGBFRS weighting plus ball-level evidence aggregation
rejected_pairs.reason: Both modules rewrite feature weights, so a remove-one ablation could not attribute the gain to either source.

performance.integration: Use VPGBFRS dependency for feature weighting; calibrate the three-way threshold on out-of-fold scores.
performance.expected_gain: >=1.0% macro-F1 over the stronger base at equal coverage
performance.kill_if: No dataset beats both bases by 1%, or the gain vanishes under remove-one ablation.

candidates.source: GBCRS (IJAR 2025) + EAC ball-level evidence, transferred to tabular classification.
candidates.claim: Ball-level evidence accumulation improves stability over a single ball cover at matched purity and block count.
candidates.search_trace: Local snapshot only; searched ball cover and evidence accumulation terms.
candidates.difference: Adds a ball-level aggregation layer; compare with a single-cover baseline and a matched random partition.
candidates.risk: More balls can overfit; matched block count and purity are required.
candidates.first_probe: Pilot 3 datasets x 3 seeds with matched m and purity.
candidates.advance_if: At least 2/3 datasets improve mean macro-F1 with lower seed variance at matched m and purity.
candidates.stop_if: Gain disappears at matched m/purity or under random-partition control.

component_sources.granular-ball cover: GBCRS (IJAR 2025): granular-ball cover construction, read from the local paper snapshot.
component_sources.ball-level evidence accumulation: EAC paper: ball-level evidence accumulation layer, read from the local paper snapshot.

rejected_pairs.pair: single-cover decision with post-hoc score rescaling
rejected_pairs.reason: Rescaling one cover's scores adds no second evidence source and is already covered by the matched-purity baseline.

rejected_pairs.pair: raising the ball count without matching purity
rejected_pairs.reason: More balls raise purity mechanically; the gain would come from capacity, not from the evidence layer.

rejected_pairs.pair: random block partition promoted to a component
rejected_pairs.reason: The random partition is a control, not a component; folding it in would hide whether ball structure matters.

performance.integration: Replace the single-cover decision with a ball-level evidence pool; match m and purity.
performance.expected_gain: >=1.0% macro-F1 and lower seed variance at matched m/purity
performance.kill_if: No gain at matched m/purity, or random-partition control matches the hybrid.
